sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and imports
sections.what: Loads the settings file and sets up the path so the indexing engine can be found. Users see nothing here.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same setup as the other scripts, so the key is read from .env and the src folder is found.
sections.watch_out: Like app.py, it depends on being started from the project folder.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Reading options and clearing old data
sections.what: Reads the optional force flag, stops with instructions if the API key is missing, deletes the old database when force is set, and makes sure the RFP and proposal folders exist. Users see warnings for missing folders.
sections.why: The help text states that force deletes the existing database so indexing starts clean.
sections.watch_out: The force flag deletes the whole database with no confirmation, so one stray use removes all indexed content.

sections.name: main (part 2)
sections.title: Indexing and reporting results
sections.what: Stops if there are no RFP or proposal files at all, starts the search engine, indexes both folders, then prints counts of RFP chunks, proposal chunks and approach chunks.
sections.why: Likely reason: the counts let the owner confirm that the documents were read.
sections.watch_out: Running without the force flag on an existing database may add duplicate entries, but this file does not show how the engine handles repeats.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Starting the script
sections.what: Runs the main function when the file is started directly from a terminal.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard Python pattern for a runnable script.

summary: A one-time command-line script that reads the RFP and proposal files and stores their text in the search database.
purpose: Prepares the search database that the proposal app and main_workflow.py depend on.
why: The file's docstring says it must run before the workflow, so the database is built ahead of time rather than on every run. The purpose of the force option is stated in the code: to delete and rebuild.
how: Reads the optional force flag, checks the OpenAI key, deletes the old database when force is set, makes sure the input folders exist, stops if there are no files, then starts the search engine, indexes both folders, and prints chunk counts.
inputs: The optional force flag; OPENAI_API_KEY in .env; PDF files in data/rfps; PPTX files in data/proposals.
outputs: A database in data/chroma_db; printed statistics and next-step hints in the terminal.
risks: The force flag removes the entire database without asking. Indexing sends document text to OpenAI, which costs money.
debug: If it exits with a missing key message, check .env. If it reports no files, check the two folders. If indexing fails, a traceback is printed. If the statistics show zero chunks, nothing was read. If the proposal app still says not indexed, confirm data/chroma_db was created.
